title: LMCache/LMCache Release v0.5.3rc2 · ROCm (gfx942, gfx950)
event_hint: LMCache v0.5.3rc2 ROCm wheel for AMD Instinct gfx942/gfx950
problem: AMD Instinct deployments need an LMCache build with matching ROCm, Python, PyTorch, and vLLM ABI versions to run KV-cache infrastructure reliably.
mechanism: The release publishes a ROCm 7.2 LMCache v0.5.3rc2 wheel for gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) and gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X), ABI-matched to the upstream vllm/vllm-openai-rocm image with torch 2.11 and CPython 3.12. Installation uses pip with --no-deps and a versioned GitHub expanded-assets link.

evidence.claim: A ROCm 7.2 wheel is available for LMCache v0.5.3rc2.
The wheel supports AMD Instinct gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) and gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X), with ABI matching to torch 2.11/cp312 in the upstream vLLM ROCm image.
The release documents pip installation with --no-deps and the matching expanded-assets URL.

evaluation_context: This is an official LMCache packaging release for AMD/ROCm. It records architecture and software compatibility targets and an install command, but no KV-cache transfer volume, latency, throughput, or network-utilization data.
limitations: The release candidate does not establish performance or compatibility beyond the specified ROCm, accelerator, PyTorch, Python, and vLLM versions. It is an older release candidate relative to v0.5.3rc4 and cannot by itself show which changes are functional rather than packaging-only. The page contains GitHub loading-error placeholders around the short body.
project_relevance: This provides a reproducible AMD/ROCm environment for LMCache KV-cache experiments, but should be treated as an installation prerequisite rather than evidence of improved network scheduling or token latency (inference).
source_notes: Facts extracted from the fetched official LMCache GitHub release page; title copied exactly from input metadata.
No performance claims were inferred from the packaging release.
